# iced (vendored)

- **Upstream:** https://github.com/iced-rs/iced
- **Revision:** `8ff48c42b0d5188223501ea1ccc506fd5beaf36a`
- **Copied:** 2026-11-06, from the checkout cargo had fetched for this revision (decision N2, `docs/native/decisions/0002-vendored-iced.md`).
- **Left out:** `examples/`, `benches/`, `docs/`, `tests/` and each crate's `tests/`, `.cargo/`, `.github/`, `Cargo.lock`, `Cross.toml`, the roadmap, contributing and dependency notes, `clippy.toml`.
- **Manifest edits:** the root `Cargo.toml` lost its `[[bench]]` targets, `[dev-dependencies]` and the `examples/*` workspace member; `widget/Cargo.toml` lost its `[dev-dependencies]`. The crates still inherit `workspace = true` dependencies from that root, and the root's `[workspace.dependencies]` still names `winit`, `cryoglyph` and `cosmic-text` by git URL: `engine/Cargo.toml` patches those URLs to the copies beside it.

Licences are kept as shipped. Every source file the crates compile, and every file they `include_bytes!`/`include_str!`, is present.

## Local fixes

None yet. Each fix to this copy gets an entry here: what changed, why, and the upstream issue or pull request link, so
that the copy can be replaced by a newer upstream revision without losing or forgetting a fix.

- **K-stage, host GPU instance policy** (`wgpu/src/instance.rs`, `wgpu/src/lib.rs`, `wgpu/src/window/compositor.rs`): a startup-installed function supplies ordered instance descriptors, without introducing an engine dependency into iced. Windowed and headless compositors try the entire adapter/device negotiation for each descriptor; failures retain diagnostics. StykAnimate supplies its existing native backend/compiler policy (DX12 with FXC first where available, fallback and environment overrides). Headless device limits retain the adapter's resolution and the default bind-group count so the stage and UI share one device. Upstream issue: none (application integration hook).

- **S2a: a key's whole text is inserted.** `core/src/text/editor.rs` (`Binding::Type`, `Edit::Type`, `from_key_press`). The default binding inserted only the first character of a key press's text, so a key that yields two scalars (the Arabic lam-alef key, dead-key results) lost the rest. Upstream issue: none found (searched 2026-11-07).
- **S2a: intake before mutation.** `core/src/text/editor.rs` (`Intake`, `Room`), `core/src/text/input.rs` (`set_intake`, `admit`, `room`), `widget/src/text_input.rs` (`.intake`). Typed text, pastes, IME commits and **Enter** are cut to the field's limits before the editor edits, shapes or records history, with the editor's context (its size in characters, the selection, and the distinct UTF-16 units when asked); an edit that takes nothing is not an edit. Admission borrows the pasted text (no copy before it is cut). Upstream filtered after the edit (`on_input`), so a huge paste was allocated and shaped first, Enter bypassed any limit and a rejection round trip cleared history. Upstream issue: none found.
- **S2a: bounded, coalesced field history, Ctrl+Shift+Z.** `graphics/src/text/editor.rs` (`History`, `seal_history`), `core/src/text/editor.rs` (`from_key_press`, `Editor::seal_history`), `core/src/text/input.rs`. One typing run is one undo step (continuing insertions within one second, at most 1,024 items); moving the caret, selecting, clicking and leaving the field end the group; the history holds 200 changes and 1 MiB of text; an external `overwrite` clears it; Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes. Upstream: unbounded, one step per keystroke, no Ctrl+Shift+Z, no group boundaries. Upstream issue: none found.
- **S2a: clipboard replies carry the request's ID, and clipboard work is bounded.** `core/src/clipboard.rs` (`RequestId`, `Event::Read(result, id)`, `Clipboard::reads`, `MAX_TEXT_BYTES`, `cancel`, `take_cancelled`), `core/src/shell.rs` (`read_clipboard_as`), `winit/src/clipboard.rs` (one worker thread, a queue of 8, `ClipboardOccupied` when it is full, cancelled reads skipped, text cut to 1 MiB on the worker), `winit/src/lib.rs` (`run_clipboard`), `core/src/text/editor.rs` (`pending_paste`, `Update::Paste(id)`, the paste cut again to 1 MiB). The reply identified only the window, so a paste started in field A landed in whichever field had focus when it arrived, and every request spawned a thread waiting on the clipboard's mutex. An editor takes only the reply to its own request, only while focused, one request at a time; losing focus cancels it. Upstream issue: none found.
- **S2a: focus, composition, key policy and identity on `TextInput`.** `widget/src/text_input.rs` (`on_focus_change` reported before the event that follows it, `on_compose`, `key_binding`, `base_direction`; `diff` resets the state of a field whose ID changed and unfocuses one that is disabled; a field without `on_input` is not focusable), `core/src/text/editor.rs` (`State::is_composing`; losing focus clears the composition and cancels the pending paste; `Update::Handled` for a copy or cut with nothing selected and for a second paste while one is pending, so the key reaches nobody else), `core/src/text/input.rs` (`Layout::base_direction`, an RTL placeholder aligned right, a one-line field selects its text when an operation gives it focus), `graphics/src/text/editor.rs` (`set_base_direction`). A role's Enter/Escape policy, focus reporting, composition reporting, a forced bidi base direction and a field's lifetime need these. Upstream issue: none found.
- **S2a: caret position in right-to-left lines.** `graphics/src/text/editor.rs` (`selection`). The visual line holding the caret was found from the first and last glyph's byte indices, which are the wrong ends in a right-to-left line (underflow of `i - 1` at index 0), the caret x summed glyph widths left to right, and the caret of an empty right-to-left field was at the left. It now uses `cosmic_text::caret_x_at` and `extent_end` (one pass over the line's glyphs), and an empty field with a right-to-left base direction starts at its right edge. Upstream issue: none found.
- **S2a: the editor trims the shaped-run cache.** `graphics/src/text/editor.rs` (`perform` ends with `shape_run_cache.trim(1024)`): words not used for 1,024 edits leave the cache of shaped words that makes a long paragraph cheap to edit (see `vendor/cosmic-text/VENDOR.md`). Upstream never trims it. Upstream issue: none found.
- **S2a: presents are recorded on request.** New `winit/src/presents.rs`, `winit/src/lib.rs`. A check that times keystroke to presentation needs the instant the surface was presented; recording is off until `presents::start()`. Upstream issue: none (a measurement hook).
- **S2t, typography on `Font`** (`core/src/font.rs`, `graphics/src/text.rs`, `graphics/src/text/{paragraph,cache}.rs`): `Weight::Value(u16)` (any `wght`), `Font::optical_size` (`Default` or `Auto`, resolved from the logical text size by `to_attributes_sized`), `Font::features` (OpenType tags, forwarded to the shaper) and `Font::tracking` (thousandths of an em, cosmic-text's `letter_spacing`); all are part of the paragraph cache key because `Font` is hashed. `to_attributes(font)` stays for the editor and input (another spike's files) and leaves `Auto` at the default coordinate. Why: the interface uses weights 450, 650 and 760, `tnum`, tracking and Inter's optical size, which the nine named weights and an attribute-less `Font` cannot express.
- **S2t, `text::font_system_if_built()`** (`graphics/src/text.rs`): the global font system as a plain `static` that can be asked, without building it, whether it exists. Why: building it scans every installed font; the program builds it on a worker and lets the interface thread touch it only after (`styk_design::warm_up`).
- **S2t, `Shaping::Auto` for fonts that need full shaping** (`graphics/src/text.rs`, `to_shaping(shaping, text, font)`): `Auto` chooses the basic shaper only for ASCII text in a font with no OpenType features and no named family. The basic shaper applies no feature and no kerning, so a default `text("0123456789")` in a bundled family with `tnum` was laid out proportionally and unkerned while the browser shapes it in full.

- **S2c, text rendering state and grayscale scopes** (`graphics/src/text.rs`, `wgpu/src/{layer,geometry,text}.rs`, `wgpu/src/lib.rs`, `wgpu/src/window/compositor.rs`, `tiny_skia/src/*`): `graphics::text::{Rendering, SubpixelOrder, set_rendering, rendering}` is the program-wide setting (subpixel order, coverage adjustment); `Text::{Paragraph, Editor, Cached}` carry `grayscale`, set from the thread's `Grayscale` scope when the text is drawn (canvas text is always grayscale, as in the browser); the wgpu text pipeline asks cryoglyph for subpixel text unless the text is grayscale, and the device requests `DUAL_SOURCE_BLENDING` where the adapter has it (windows and headless). The tiny-skia renderer ignores the flag.
- **S2d, glyphs drawn off the interface thread** (`graphics/src/text.rs`, `wgpu/src/text.rs`): `Rendering` has `direct_write`; `graphics::text::{install_glyph_source, glyphs_pending, set_glyph_notifier}` carry cryoglyph's worker state to the program (the wgpu text pipeline installs it when it is built); a cached text upload whose frame left glyphs out (`TextRenderer::incomplete`) is prepared again on the next frame, so glyphs that arrived are drawn without any change in the interface.
- **S2e, frames are withheld until their glyphs are drawn** (`wgpu/src/presentation.rs`, `wgpu/src/lib.rs`, `wgpu/src/text.rs`, `wgpu/src/window/compositor.rs`, `graphics/src/text.rs`, `graphics/src/compositor.rs`, `winit/src/lib.rs`): `Renderer::prepare` is a cryoglyph candidate (`begin_candidate`/`end_candidate`); `Renderer::hold_frame` (a `presentation::Gate`) says, after a frame is drawn, whether the window keeps its last complete frame because the text lacks glyphs a worker is still drawing, for at most `presentation::LIMIT`; the wgpu compositor now prepares the frame first (`Renderer::prepare_candidate`), asks the gate, and only then acquires the surface's texture and draws (`show_candidate`); a held frame is submitted without drawing (`drop_candidate`) and the compositor returns the new `SurfaceError::Withheld(until)`, which iced_winit answers with a redraw at `until`. A texture acquired and dropped without being presented stalls the swap chain (every later acquire times out, seen on both DX12 and Vulkan), so the texture is never acquired for a frame that is not shown. `graphics::text::Rendering` has `glyphs: GlyphDrawing` and `aliased` (instead of `direct_write`); `candidate_incomplete()` tells a program that captures frames (screenshots, checks) whether the frame prepared last was whole. Why: a frame must never show text with holes.
- **S2f, no deadline, suboptimal textures, held-frame counters** (`wgpu/src/presentation.rs`, `wgpu/src/window/compositor.rs`, `wgpu/src/lib.rs`, `wgpu/src/text.rs`, `graphics/src/text.rs`, `graphics/src/compositor.rs`, `winit/src/lib.rs`): the gate no longer has a limit: an incomplete frame is never shown, and a held frame asks again after `presentation::RETRY`. `graphics::text::held_frames()` counts held candidates and waits for the developer tools. The wgpu compositor decides what to do with each answer of the swap chain in `plan`: a `Suboptimal` texture is drawn and presented and the surface is then reconfigured (new `SurfaceError::Suboptimal`, handled by iced_winit); no arm acquires a texture it does not present. The text viewport is the renderer's glyph consumer (`Renderer::glyph_state`).

- **N2, a recreated surface drops custom primitive pipelines** (`wgpu/src/primitive.rs` `Storage::clear`, `wgpu/src/engine.rs` `Engine::surface_recreated`, `wgpu/src/window/compositor.rs` `create_surface`, `wgpu/src/lib.rs` `Renderer::engine`). iced recovers a lost swap chain by creating the window's surface again (`iced_winit`: `SurfaceError::Lost`) and keeps the engine, so a custom primitive's `Pipeline` outlived the recovery and had no way to learn of it. The compositor now clears the shared pipeline storage whenever it creates a surface; each primitive makes its pipeline again on the next frame (`Pipeline::new`), which is the signal the stage uses to give its painter a new graphics context (`docs/native/stage.md`). A second window's surface does the same once, harmlessly. Upstream issue: none found.

- **K-dev panels, opt-in log sink** (`winit/src/dev_extension.rs`, `winit/Cargo.toml`): the nondefault `devtools` feature exposes a startup-only adapter to iced_winit's existing log facade. Producers use a nonblocking host sink; shipping builds omit the module and feature. This avoids introducing a second logging dependency into the app. Upstream issue: none (application integration hook).
